source.title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree

teaching.hint: Can all nodes at the requested distance be reached by following child links alone?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Distance from an interior node may travel upward and then into another subtree, so the representation must expose parent neighbors.
solution_outline.approach: Find the target and record parent links in one tree traversal. Run a breadth-first traversal from it over left, right, and parent neighbors, marking visited nodes. Return the frontier at distance k, or an empty result if the frontier expires first.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The frontier contains exactly nodes at the current distance; a visited node is never admitted again through a reverse edge.
solution_outline.correctness: Parent links supply exactly the missing directions of each tree edge. A breadth-first layer reaches all nodes with a path of that length before longer paths and first discovers each node at its shortest distance. Thus the kth layer is exactly the required set, including the target alone at k=0.
solution_outline.complexity: O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space, with early termination when no frontier remains.
solution_outline.pitfall: Without visited tracking, adding parent edges allows immediate backtracking and repeated visits.

common_wrong_turns: Without visited tracking, adding parent edges allows immediate backtracking and repeated visits.
source_fidelity_notes: Made distance directions explicit and preserved unique target-by-value identification, any output order, and k=0.
